findings.summary: The exact tri-OS candidate is not portable. resolve_safe() resolves the candidate path but compares it against an un-normalized project root. On macOS /var versus /private/var aliases and on Windows long-name versus RUNNER~1 aliases cause valid repository paths to be rejected as escapes. The macOS and Windows suites each stop with 38 setup errors; only the resource-limit and scoped-ownership tests execute successfully.

The exact candidate intentionally omits docs/roadmap/anarchy/generated/P24-001_CONTROL_PLANE_INDEX.json and the canonical refreshed SOURCE_MANIFEST.sha256. The exact Ubuntu validation report is bound to commit 365e7e7.../tree 6b9e870... and records passed=false, generatedView=MISSING, sourceManifest=DRIFT, validator=FAIL. The dedicated workflow is therefore red and the candidate is not adoption-ready.

The Worker-J-scoped schema claims an external Worker B TestExecutionResult reference but hard-codes a competing vocabulary: it omits canonical ERROR, SKIPPED, UNKNOWN, FLAKY, and NOT_IMPLEMENTED while adding SKIPPED_NOT_APPLICABLE, SKIPPED_WITH_REASON, FLAKY_QUARANTINED, UNKNOWN_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED, and CANCELLED. Result state and reason/classification must remain separate and the reference must match the canonical Worker B v1 state domain exactly.

Independent adoption review remains incomplete. This artifact supplies Worker B’s exact-head decision, but Worker I exact-head review is still absent; the candidate’s own report correctly keeps independentReviews=BLOCKED. No adoption or authority promotion may occur until the next exact candidate has both required reviews and no high/critical finding.

On Ubuntu, all 15 deterministic tests pass, including active-claim and shared-contract collision rejection, safe takeover/yield continuity, clean-room Worker J resume, atomic-write interruption safety, non-mutating check mode, source-manifest generator idempotence, bounded/honest generated reporting, and P2/source-to-behavior status-inflation rejection.

The candidate preserves one human authority and one bounded machine authority, does not promote PR #63 or v3.2 references, labels generated navigation as non-authoritative, keeps task/worker/test/certification/capability domains separate, pins exact candidate checkout, and does not edit Worker A, Worker B, Worker C, or product runtime scope.
